title: Non-pressure playing and wet lips
summary: Metoyer did not push the non-pressure system on young Ernie, wanting him to build lip muscle. He used it himself when tired from jitney dances and favored playing with moist lips.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: That was your four. I've heard that Arnaud Mottwey was famous for his non-pressure playing. He could walk up to a trumpet like hanging on a string and lower things like that. You could do that. Did he ever stress that in his lessons? That was not for you, not the first measure? Did he do anything special to teach you that?

Well, no. He didn't actually stress to me about the non-pressure system of playing. Even when he started me on double-tonging and triple-tonging, he wanted me to use... By me being so young, he wanted me to build the muscles up in my lips. See, that was the general idea. The non-pressure system, you don't use much muscles, you see. And he wanted me to build the muscles up in my lips. So he wanted me to play the natural way. Which he could play both ways, you understand? Yeah. But he mostly used the non-pressure system like he was playing the jitney house on the music box on Canal and Crudlin at that time.

And after playing them jitneys there for maybe six, seven hours, they'd play all night in the air for the day. When he'd get tired, he'd start playing in the non-pressure system and just like starting all over, see. His lips wouldn't get tired.
Did he say anything about playing with wet lips or dry lips or anything like that?

No, he was more in favor of playing with your lips wet, see. That moist lips keep from cracking. You see, dry lips, what actually happens, I could say it in a lot of time, your throat gets dry too. And your mouthpiece, nine out of ten, will stick to your lip. And if you move it, well, you slip off your armature, you see. Where they're wet, they're not going to slip off your armature. All you would have to leave your lips stay wet and just wipe their mouthpiece off and put it right back, see. And it'll fall right back in place.
